cards.title: Disagreeing on direction
cards.prompt: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a technical direction your team or a senior person wanted to take.
follow_ups: What did the other person believe, and why?
What did you do to test who was right?
What changed someone's mind, yours or theirs?
How was your working relationship afterwards?
Looking back, were you right?
strong_answer_covers: States the other view fairly, at its strongest
Uses data, a prototype or a written proposal rather than volume
A clear outcome, including the case where they lost and committed anyway
The relationship after the disagreement
Describes a real disagreement and reaches the other person directly, not around them
red_flags: Story details change when probed, showing the experience was invented

cards.title: Something that went wrong
cards.prompt: Tell me about something you shipped that didn't go to plan.
follow_ups: When did you first know something was wrong?
What part of it was yours?
What did you do in the first hour?
What changed in how you or the team work afterwards?
How did you tell the people affected?
strong_answer_covers: Notices early or explains why they didn't
Owns their part without hiding behind the team
Concrete fix plus a process change that stuck
Clear impact, ideally with a number
Does not shift blame to another team or a tool

cards.title: Improving how the team works
cards.prompt: Describe a time you improved how your team works without anyone asking you to.
follow_ups: Why you, and why then?
Who resisted, and why?
How did you get people to actually adopt it?
How did you measure whether it helped?
Is it still in use?
strong_answer_covers: A real problem they noticed themselves
Scope that matches the level
Brought others along rather than imposing it
Adoption or impact numbers
red_flags: Story details change when probed, showing the experience was invented

cards.title: Hard feedback
cards.prompt: What's the hardest feedback you've received, and what did you do with it?
follow_ups: How did you react in the moment?
What did you do differently the next week?
How did you know the change worked?
Have you given similar feedback to someone else since?
strong_answer_covers: Specific feedback, not a disguised strength
No defensiveness in the retelling
A visible change in behaviour, with an example
Picks feedback that stung, not a disguised strength, and does not relitigate it
red_flags: Story details change when probed, showing the experience was invented

cards.title: Working through ambiguity
cards.prompt: Tell me about a time you had to deliver something when the requirements were unclear or kept changing.
follow_ups: What did you do first to reduce the uncertainty?
Who did you go to, and what did you ask?
What did you decide without waiting for an answer?
What would you do differently?
strong_answer_covers: Takes action to reduce ambiguity: questions, a prototype, a written proposal
Makes reasonable decisions and records the assumptions
Delivers something useful and adjusts
Does not wait to be told or blame whoever wrote the requirements
red_flags: Story details change when probed, showing the experience was invented

cards.title: Helping someone grow
cards.prompt: Tell me about a time you helped a teammate get unblocked or grow in their role.
follow_ups: What was getting in their way?
What did you do, and what did you deliberately not do?
How did you know it worked?
What did you learn about helping people?
strong_answer_covers: Diagnoses the real blocker
Coaches rather than doing the work for them
A visible outcome for the other person
